title: Tiered SLO guardrails and smart page suppression to reduce noisy paging
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: on-call noise is increasing due to a flood of transient alerts tied to tail-latency spikes and regional capacity throttles. These alerts are drowning out real multi-region SLO incidents and increasing MTTR. Goal: implement a tiered SLO-driven alerting pipeline with smart suppression, automated mitigation playbooks, and circuit-breaker triggers to reduce pages by ~60% while keeping P0 visibility for genuine customer-impacting events. This ticket covers design, runbook templates, automation hooks, and an initial staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Total pages during normal traffic reduced by >=60% compared to baseline week
P0 pages only fire for global SLO breaches or confirmed multi-region failover events
Automated mitigations trigger for P1 events and resolve or create incident with incident-id in <=10 minutes
Runbook runner executes rollback or load-shed actions via feature flag and records audit log to S3/KMS
Regression test (chaos + synthetic traffic) validates suppression and circuit-breaker behavior in staging
implementation_plan: 1) Define SLO tiers and mapping to paging tiers: global-critical (P0), regional-critical (P1), transient/variance (P2)
2) Implement alert enrichment pipeline: attach slo_context (global vs regional), last_incident_id, kv_cache_hit_rate, request_qps, and model_variant to alerts before routing
3) Add dedupe and suppression rules: 5min suppression for identical alert signature if automated mitigation in-flight; incremental backoff for noisy sources
4) Circuit-breaker hooks: when regional error-rate > 5% and sustained for 3m, flip regional-circuit to 'degraded' and reroute to other regions; escalate to P1 page
5) Load-shedding policy: define graceful shedding buckets (low-priority background tasks, embedding batch windows) and implement via router feature flags with automatic rollback on error
6) Runbook automation: author canonical runbook templates for P0/P1/P2 with playbook steps, automated steps, manual checkpoints, and one-click remediation buttons in Console
7) Integrations: PagerDuty automation playbooks, GitHub PR automation for hotfix rollbacks, and Slack incident channel templating
8) Testing: synthetic SLO breach in staging, chaos injectors to validate circuit-breaker and shed behavior, and tabletop with on-call team
9) Gradual rollout: enable for non-critical customer traffic for 1 week, expand to 50% traffic in beta, then full rollout behind a runtime feature flag
10) Post-rollout: monitor pages, adjust thresholds, and ship postmortem with metrics to reliability dashboard
progress_notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with SRE, Platform, and Console teams. Agreed on three-tier SLO mapping and that P0 requires multi-region or customer-visible error surface.
2026-02-22: Drafted runbook templates in Confluence (link below). Decided automated mitigations should have a manual-confirm step for P0 only.
2026-03-02: Prototype suppression middleware implemented that enriches alerts with slo_context and dedupe key. Early tests in staging reduced duplicates by ~40%.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Design. Console UX for 'one-click mitigate' added; security asked for KMS-wrapped audit logs for automated actions.
2026-03-10: PagerDuty automation playbook prototype created (PD-Playbook-42). First automated rollback via GH Actions simulated in staging and logged properly.

2026-03-12: Started gated rollout to internal services traffic flag=beta. Observed 52% reduction in pages for internal runs during 24h window. No regressions so far. Moving to expand coverage next week.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive suppression risks hiding slow-developing incidents; mitigated by requiring SLO trend correlation and automatic re-escalation if suppression thresholds are exceeded.
We chose to keep P0 manual confirmation for any global SLO remediation to avoid automated changes that could worsen incidents.
Next steps: finalize suppression heuristic parameters and schedule tabletop incident drill for March 24th.
